prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have moved from base editing alone to a two-part prize. B052 is the most robust case on the table: three decades of independent confirmation, a clean two-person attribution, and a real mechanistic basis in ligand design and the steps of oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination. In round 1 I said I would listen if Somfai showed that the C-N advance is independent of the 2010 prize, and he did: general, ligand-controlled catalysts for a bond type the 2010 citation did not cover is new chemistry and not a substrate-scope extension. B004 remains my own scientific preference. A programmable DNA-binding step is coupled to defined deaminase chemistry on a single nucleotide, avoiding the break-driven repair that makes Cas9 outcomes heterogeneous, and the adenine editor required evolving a deaminase that has no natural DNA substrate. It has been reproduced in many laboratories and cell types. Pairing a mature synthetic method with a biomolecular tool is, to my mind, a fair statement of where chemistry changed what researchers can do, and it fits the three-person cap as two plus one.
statement.case_against: The cost of this configuration is that Komor and Gaudelli are not named, although their first-author work on the cytosine and adenine editors was specific and decisive, and I said in round 1 that I would resist dropping them. I accept it only because the cap forces the choice and because crediting the laboratory head with a citation naming the invention, not an editor class, is the least unfair option; it is a real concession. Base editing is also still close to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and long-term safety and clinical outcome data (off-target deamination, bystander edits, durability) are still emerging, so a committee could reasonably judge B004 early. B052 carries the Kosugi priority question and the sequel-to-2010 objection, and a mixed two-part prize risks reading as a compromise between two camps rather than two prizes each justified on their own.

responses.point: Argued that the ligand design and mechanistic work behind Pd-catalysed C-N coupling were new chemistry and not a substrate-scope extension of the 2010 prize, while conceding that omitting Kosugi invites a priority argument and that he does not currently prefer a biology-facing second part.
responses.response: This is the argument I said in round 1 I needed, and it moves me: the general catalysts and the mechanistic understanding behind them are a separate achievement from C-C coupling. I do not agree that a biology-facing second part should be excluded. A single B052 prize is the safe, unobjectionable choice, but I would rather the committee also recognise the one candidate where a biological process was turned into a defined chemical reaction. On Kosugi, my own reading is that the tin-amide reaction was a precursor and not the general, ligand-controlled method, so a citation worded around the general palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is defensible. Like Zou, I am working from the files and cannot check the original papers, and I would want that stated openly in the record.

responses.point: Proposed pairing B052 (Buchwald, Hartwig) with B004 credited to Liu alone, as a balanced prize of a mature synthetic method and a newer biomolecular tool, with the three-person cap allocated as two plus one.
responses.response: I have come to the same configuration, but I want to be clear that I get there from the other side. In round 1 I resisted dropping Komor or Gaudelli, and I still think their editors are distinct achievements. I accept Liu alone because the cap leaves no alternative that keeps a two-part prize, and because the citation names base editing as the invention rather than any single editor class. I would not frame the pairing as balance for its own sake; each part has to stand on its own evidence. B052 does on thirty years of confirmation. B004 does on mechanism and independent reproduction. I share your doubt about the closeness to the 2020 prize and about early clinical data, and I do not think those disappear by being paired with an older method.

responses.point: Proposed a single-part B002 prize for Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, with a citation covering liquid-liquid phase separation and the multivalency principles, while acknowledging that physiological relevance is disputed and that Pappu and Mittag are excluded.
responses.response: The chair's own reservation is the one I keep returning to: much of the cellular evidence rests on overexpression and imaging, and I have seen in my own field how a widely held assumption about dNTP levels changed once it was measured quantitatively. A citation anchored on the physical concept and the in vitro reconstitution would be defensible, but the in vivo claims would not be, and I cannot tell from the files how cleanly the committee could draw that line. I keep B002 as an alternative and not in my configuration. Rosen's multivalency work is the strongest part of it, and I would reconsider if the committee could show that the 2009 droplet result has been quantitatively confirmed in cells at endogenous expression levels.

responses.point: Proposed B009, long-range electron transfer in proteins, for Gray and Winkler as a mature, quantitative mechanism, while declaring closeness to the field and acknowledging the Marcus, Hopfield, Dutton and Moser overlap.
responses.response: I respect the quantitative rigour, and the chair asks whether a second member who is not close to the field could support it. I cannot, on what is before me: the question of who established what, between Marcus, Hopfield, Dutton and Moser and Gray and Winkler, is unresolved in the files, and I would not credit two names with a field that others built in parallel. As a biochemist I would be glad to see the priority sorted out in a future cycle, but I am not moving B009 into my configuration or my alternatives this round.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts Liu alone for B004, and whether Komor and Gaudelli, or Nishida and Kondo with Target-AID, should displace him; I cannot settle the conception of each editor class from the files.
Whether Kosugi's tin-amide work was general and ligand-controlled enough to share B052; my reading is that it was not, but I have not checked the original papers.
How much weight to give the 2020 CRISPR prize and the still-emerging clinical safety data as arguments to wait on base editing.
Whether a mixed two-part prize is better than the single B052 prize that more members prefer.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: I have no stated personal or institutional connection to Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo, Nishida or Kosugi. My field of DNA replication and genome stability is close to the topic of base editing, which affects my judgement but is not a recusal issue. The Umeå and Stockholm committee context does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
